answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity tend its own orchard: reputation grows only through a serial chain of small useful tasks, each step hashed from the last, so a thousand fake accounts cannot be run in parallel on one machine. Each chain starts from a kernel of earned work that ripens slowly, like fruit over seasons, and every completed harvest is carved into an onyx ledger that peers can audit. Cloning an identity restarts the whole season from zero, so the cost of each fake grows with every alias while honest agents keep their ripened standing.
